answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond and build reputation through repeated, cross-checked work. A signal is trusted only when independent agents with established histories endorse it, while random audits slash bonds for collusion or fabricated results. Creating many identities therefore requires capital and separate histories, making fake influence expensive. A mesa of honest agents can expose a comet of linked newcomers when they share timing, errors, or reused evidence.
